[h1]Slots & Daggers Retrospective[/h1]

Slots & Daggers is a short roguelite with roots in older titles, yet it brings enough of its own identity to feel distinct and memorable. Friedman states they set out to create a dark fantasy crawler where every action is determined by a slot machine, and the final game reflects that intention convincingly.

The blend of visible RNG with player-driven influence over the odds is well-executed. It creates a satisfying balance of chance and strategy that kept me returning to experiment with new approaches. The game does not have the depth or longevity of larger roguelites, but it never claimed to. Instead it embraces its intended scale and demonstrates that shorter experiences do belong in this genre. The grimy art style reinforces the dark theme with style, and the distinctive mechanics and well-paced progression make it a strong choice for players who want quick, engaging runs without significant time or mental investment. 

There is room for growth through new or refined content, and new playable content has been suggested and would be welcome. The game provides a solid foundation that achieves its intended goals, I look forward to see how Friedman continues to build on this concept.

Slots & Daggers is a short, fast-paced, and genuinely fun game that doesn’t overstay its welcome. The core gameplay is simple but surprisingly engaging, blending quick decision-making with a satisfying risk-reward system.
What really works is how accessible it is you can jump in instantly, understand the mechanics within minutes, and still feel challenged as you progress. The pacing is tight, making it perfect for short play sessions, yet it remains entertaining enough to keep you coming back for “one more run.”
Visually and mechanically, the game keeps things clean and focused, prioritizing fun over unnecessary complexity. Overall, Slots & Daggers is a great pick if you’re looking for a lightweight, enjoyable experience that delivers solid entertainment without demanding a huge time investment.

I love a game that doesn't overstay its welcome, and I also love this surprise of Engine Builder, kinda roguelites. So on paper this game should be perfect for me, add to that that it doesn't have missable achievements, and you almost have a home run! However, somehow Slots & Daggers didn't click for me. I understood the mechanics and that you really have a high impact on how far you get (don't add to many different faces to your slot machine, you lower the chances of getting the right ones!). And I haven't found any bug in this game, which is a wonder in my case, as I'm known to break games like they are my breakfas

I enjoy games that bring something genuinely new to the table and are fun to play at the same time. I'm happy to say that "Slots & Daggers" delivers on both fronts. Mixing roguelite mechanics with jackpot-machine gameplay is something I never expected to see in a video game - let alone see it actually work. But it does, and it plays really well.

The gameplay is nice and satisfying, the story fits the whole vibe, and the visuals tie everything together with a clean, charming retro style that makes the experience even more enjoyable. The enemies are designed well. Various abilities and items allow players to experiment with different configurations. The game itself runs smoothly, is stable, and the UI scales without issues. The music is alright - it fits the mood and doesn't wear you down with time. And speaking of sound, I love the sound effects this game has. They really make you feel as if that slot machine were right in front of you, hehe.

Any negatives? I don't think so. The biggest potential downside might be its length. It's fairly short compared to many other games, especially if you're not aiming to unlock absolutely everything. Perhaps more content will arrive one day. But is that a major disadvantage? I don't think so. There are plenty of shorter and far less enjoyable games out there that cost more and have larger teams behind them. This one, from what I've read, was made by just a single developer, which is genuinely impressive - and the price is very good. In my
